title: Desperate-Dan/WaSSPipe
description: Consensus generation and analysis pipeline for the WaSPP project (WIP).

input_options.title: Input Options
input_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and change some frequently used options.

fastq.title: FASTQ
fastq.description: Provide the path to the fastq_pass directory for your run.
fastq.help_text: This should be the the path the the fastq_pass folder, which should contain a folder for each barcode in your run. This expects your data to be demultiplexed already, you will need to do that through Minknow if it is not already demultiplexed.

ref.title: Reference file
ref.description: The reference file your samples will be mapped against for reference based assembly (default: WaSPP curated viral family references).
ref.help_text: Change this to a custom reference file to map your samples against. The default contains all NCBI reference sequences for the members of the viral families of interest to the WaSPP project.

depth.title: Read depth
depth.description: Positions below this depth will be masked in the resulting consensus sequences (default: 20).
depth.help_text: When generating a consensus sequence, if there are less than this number of reads at that position it will be replaced with an N. The base quality (see below) is considered when counting the read depth at a position.

baseQ.title: Base Quality
baseQ.description: Change the minimum base quality threshold (default: 20).
baseQ.help_text: If a base quality score is below this value it won't be considered as part of the count for read depth.

read_count.title: Read Count
read_count.description: The minimum number of reads mapping to a reference to be considered for consensus generation (default: 50).
read_count.help_text: After mapping to your reference(s) of choice, if a given reference has at least this number of reads mapped to it WaSSPipe will try to generate a consensus sequence for it. The mapping quality of these reads (see below) is considered when read counting.

mappingQ.title: Mapping Quality
mappingQ.description: Change the minimum read mapping quality threshold (default: 15).
mappingQ.help_text: If the read mapping quality is below this threshold it won't be considered as part of the count for minimum read count.

max_len.title: Maximum read length
max_len.description: Reads above this length will be filtered before read mapping (deafult: 1500bp).
max_len.help_text: Standard WaSPP primers shouldn't generate a fragment longer than 1500bp.

min_len.title: Minimum read length
min_len.description: Reads below this length will be filtered before read mapping (default: 100bp).

trim_len.title: Trim length
trim_len.description: Number of bases to trim from the ends of the reads to remove primers (default: 30bp).
trim_len.help_text: Currently WaSPP primers are not longer than 30bp, so trimming this length should remove primer sequences from downstream analysis.

parse_all.title: Parse all folders in the fastq_pass folder
parse_all.description: By default the pipeline will only process folders in the fastq_pass directory that start with 'barcode'
parse_all.help_text: but if you want to parse all folders in the fastq_pass directory (if you want to include 'Unclassified' or have folders starting with something other than 'barcode') you can tick this box. WARNING: processing the 'Unclassified' folder can significantly increase the runtime and memory usage!

database.title: Kraken2 Database
database.description: Change the database to use for Kraken2 read assignment (deafult: Viral).
database.help_text: NB VIRAL IS THE ONLY OPTION CURRENTLY AVAILABLE, BUT THIS WILL CHANGE IN THE FUTURE IF OTHER DATABASES ARE ADDED TO THE PIPELINE.

individual_krona.title: Individual Krona plots
individual_krona.description: Choose whether to generate individual krona plots for each sample or not (default: False).

miscellaneous_options.title: Miscellaneous Options
miscellaneous_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.
